title: Adaptive phase-draining with kernel-suitability ranking and tenant-aware fairness
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: We observe recurring p95/p99 latency spikes for mixed tenant workloads when kernel suitability shifts mid-request (e.g., prefill that would benefit from a sparse-attention kernel flows into decode that prefers dense kernels). The current scheduler treats a phase boundary as an opaque cut; draining microbatches from one kernel to another can either (a) cause queueing that worsens tail latency or (b) force execution on a suboptimal kernel that increases per-token cost. We need a scheduler policy that (1) scores kernel suitability per-phase, (2) drains or migrates work in a controlled way, and (3) enforces proportional fairness across tenants and latency-sensitive requests.
motivation: Improve tail latency without sacrificing throughput for bursty multi-tenant traffic. Reduce customer-visible spikes and improve predictable SLO attainment, while keeping cost increases minimal. Enable smoother transitions when kernel selection changes near phase boundaries and avoid tenant starvation during drain events.
proposed_solution: 1) Compute a lightweight kernel_suitability_score at request admission and at phase transition. Score components: sequence_length_expectation, attention_sparsity_hint, kv_cache_hit_ratio, quantization_profile_penalty, tenant_priority. 2) Introduce an adaptive phase-draining component that: - Ranks in-flight microbatches by kernel_suitability_score delta and tenant-weighted latency urgency. - Allows soft-migration: if migrating to a better kernel would reduce p99 by >X% and migration cost < threshold, perform migration; otherwise, drain on current kernel with hedging windows. 3) Fairness: implement proportional token shares per-tenant within latency buckets. Use token-credits that decay on latency violations to prioritize at-risk tenants. 4) Safety: fallback to current allocator on instability; limit migrations to a small concurrency cap per GPU to avoid thrash.
design_decisions: - Use a single scalar kernel_suitability_score to keep admission path cheap. - Score computed in serving runtime (C++ hot path) with precomputed model hints from the model catalog to avoid per-request heavy ops. - Migration decisions are opportunistic and bounded (max 5% of active microbatches per device). - Tenant fairness is enforced with proportional shares rather than strict priorities to avoid head-of-line blocking.
tradeoffs: - Benefits: lower p99 for mixed workloads, better resource utilization when kernels align with work. - Costs: added orchestration complexity, slight CPU overhead for scoring, and potential kernel switch overheads. - Risk of oscillation if scores are noisy; mitigated by smoothing and hysteresis windows.
implementation_plan: Phase A (spike): implement kernel_suitability_score and telemetry hooks + simulation harness that replays production traces. Phase B (dev): implement draining controller and migration path in runtime with unit/integration tests. Phase C (canary): enable on dedicated pool 5% traffic, monitor. Phase D (ramp): 25% -> 100% with rollout gates.
metrics_and_alerting: Primary metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (prefill, decode), tokens/sec, kernel-switch-rate, mean GPU utilization, tenant slowdown ratio (95th). Acceptance: p99 improvement >= 8% for mixed small-seq workloads under same throughput and kernel cost delta < 2%. Alert if kernel-switch-rate > configured threshold or if throughput drops > 1%.
experiment_plan: 1) Offline: run scheduler simulator across 7 days of ta3 cluster traces. 2) Dev: unit tests + microbench harness that measures migration overhead. 3) Canary: route 5% of traffic in staging-like dedicated pool and compare against control for 48h. 4) Gradual ramp if steady.
rollout_and_rollback: Canary toggle via runtime flag. Rollback immediate if p99 regresses by >5% or if error rates increase. Use automatic fallback to existing allocator for affected devices.
acceptance_criteria: - p99 (decode) reduced by >=8% on target workloads during canary. - No >1% drop in overall throughput. - No tenant sees >10% increased violation rate compared to baseline. - No production incidents attributable to scheduler for 72 hours post-rollout.
testing: Unit tests for score computation, deterministic migration decision tests, integration tests with mock kernels, load test in CI that simulates tenant mixes. Smoke runbook for on-call with playbook steps and dashboards linked.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy score leads to oscillation -> mitigation: exponential smoothing + minimum time window. Risk: kernel-switch thrash -> mitigation: per-device migration cap and backoff. Risk: fairness regressions -> mitigation: conservative share tuning and shadowing for 2 weeks before enforcement.
next_steps: 1) Finish canary preflight and allocate staging traffic slice. 2) Run 48h canary and capture metrics. 3) Adjust scores/hysteresis based on canary results and iterate. 4) Prepare runtime-1.22 release notes and operational runbook.
notes: This ticket is intentionally aligned with existing phase-splitting efforts but focuses on the boundary behavior and kernel-aware migration. Coordinate with ENG-14207 (kernel probe router) and ENG-24890 (latency budget controller) for shared signals.
